children: Shares of Corvex jumped after the company said it is planning to increase its critical IT power-capacity to roughly 8 megawatts by the end of the year, up from about 1.5 megawatts currently.
The stock rose 50% to $17.20 in premarket trading Monday. Through Friday's close, shares are up nearly 78% year to date.
The AI cloud-computing company said before the bell that its more than fivefold power-capacity expansion is projected to begin generating revenue in the first quarter of 2027.

The expansion involves doubling capacity at Corvex's existing Mid-Atlantic data center, where it will deploy roughly 1,000 additional graphic processing units, or GPUs. The company said it will additionally establish operations at a second existing enterprise-scale data center in the Midwest, where it will deploy about 2,000 latest-generation GPUs.
Corvex will look to continue to scale its power capacity in the coming years, with Co-Founder and Co-CEO Jay Crystal noting the company has the right to scale to more than 20 megawatts in 2027.
Corvex said it will fund the expansions with proceeds from a private placement of common stock and Series D Preferred Stock, led by Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and Oppenheimer.
